translation: In general, wheezing must give rise to distension, and distension must give rise to wheezing. The formularies hold that when wheezing precedes distension one treats the lung, and when distension precedes wheezing one treats the spleen; this too is an established view.

The Jingui has wind edema, skin edema, stone edema, true edema, and yellow sweat, dividing treatment by exterior and interior; Hejian has the three-burner separate-dispersing method; Zihe has grinding accumulations and expelling water. All have profound meaning. The student must immerse himself and realize it by experience; it is hard to summarize.

Looking at how the common physicians of recent times discuss water-dampness wheezing-distension, they take the Neijing's "opening the ghost gate" to induce sweating as the exterior treatment, and dividing and draining the urine to "cleanse the mansion" as the interior treatment. The Classic's meaning, in the Bingneng pian, says, "All damp swellings and fullness belong to the spleen."
